status: completed; all 16 ramp surfaces acceptable; five C bridge candidates; five identified fin failures; no accepted fin identified

user_observations.verbatim: Looking at the Mark II plate now, starting with the ramps here, I would say that my first observation is that all of them are acceptable at the surface area that we're covering here, at least.
As far as which are better or worse, it goes about as you'd expect. Smaller angles look just a little bit worse. Larger angles look just a little bit better.
For example, one of the best-looking ones is R09. One of the worst-looking ones is R05, for some reason.
I mean, it's probably tied with some others, like R01 maybe. I think R03 looks better than R01. So it does seem like generally the fan being on 100 does help a bit.
And then regarding the overhangs, I can't see anything on here that looks as good as what we had a moment ago on Mark One.
F08 and Y04 both failed. C07 failed just barely, just one thread hanging a bit low. F07 failed a bit worse than C07 but not like F08 and Y04, not nearly that bad.
Y05 (and F01) is about as bad as F08. C04 and C02 are candidates for passing. C06 and C03 maybe pass. C07 maybe passes too.

photo_assessment.source: assistant visual interpretation of eight supplied photographs, separate from user per-ID assessments
photo_assessment.specimen_id_mapping: unassigned; labels are not legible enough to identify the photographed pieces
observations: Two fin/wall assemblies show pronounced bowing in their roof regions, with long loose looped strands and locally bunched filament.
The broad fin panels appear substantially straight rather than globally buckled.
Small contact-edge remnants are irregular; a detached flat piece has a row of curled or broken-looking remnants visible in photo 3.
Detached flat pieces are visible, but the photographs do not establish how or when they separated.
photo_assessment.limits: Post-print stills do not establish whether lower teeth deformed before bridging, whether strands lost anchorage during deposition, or what damage arose during handling/removal. No photo-based fin-release acceptance or per-ID reassignment is made.
